Subject: Re: Unexpected charge in Jan invoice — possible misattributed sessions

Hi Alicia — apologies for the longer-than-expected turnaround and thanks for your patience. Summary of findings and next steps below.

What we found
- Root cause: during a provisioning script run on 2028-01-14 an internal sandbox workflow re-used ephemeral API key material which produced identical session-seed values across two tenants. Our session-to-tenant hashing routine then assigned ~19k token events to LumeSoft that should have been charged to an internal sandbox org.
- Affected window: 2028-01-14 02:00–04:15 UTC. Model variant: gpt-redwood-medium-qa. Region: us-west-2.

What we're doing now
- We have applied a provisional credit of $7,200 to LumeSoft's account and prevented collection on the disputed invoice line (you should see the credit reflected in Billing > Credits immediately).
- The tokens have been marked in our billing exports as "orphaned-misattributed" so downstream reconciliations will not reassign them to your ledger.
- Ops/Infra patch: a fix to the provisioning script and a change to the session-seed generation (introduce tenant-unique nonce) will be deployed tonight; we'll validate by replaying similar provisioning tests.

What we need from you
- If you can confirm receipt of the credit and that the invoice holds for your payment process, we'll close the case. If you need a formal credit memo or a signed adjustment, let me know and we can route a DocuSign credit memo.

References
- HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890
- Export we used: redwood-usage-ledger-snapshot-20280114.csv

Again — really sorry this happened. We'll follow up with a postmortem note once infra confirms the deployment and test results. If you'd like a quick call to walk through the ledger rows, I'm available Monday morning PST.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
